lyrics:
[Intro: acoustic guitar, whistled tune, boot stomps]

[Verse 1: laid-back male baritone, guitar and stomps]
Boss sent an email at a quarter to five
Marked it "urgent," like the building's on fire
Truck needs a belt and my back needs a break
And my thumb's got a blister from the scrolling it takes

[Pre-Chorus: fiddle slides in, drums pick up]
So I walked in the door and Darlene said, "Hon,
You know the house rule. Hand it over. Go on."

[Chorus: gang vocals, low 808 thump, fiddle hook]
Put your phone in the tip jar (hey!)
Let it buzz with the quarters and ones
Whoever's looking, let 'em look
We'll call 'em back when the night is done
Got a jukebox, got a stool, got a long old bar
So put your phone in the tip jar

[Verse 2: baritone, band grooving]
There's a plumber, a teacher, a nurse off a twelve
A kid with a ring he ain't shown to the girl
An old man toasting to a chair that's bare
We don't ask a thing, we just pull up a chair

[Pre-Chorus: fiddle climbing]
And the jar fills up like a church plate does
Darlene says, "Y'all, that's what I call love"

[Chorus: gang vocals, low 808 thump, fiddle hook]
Put your phone in the tip jar (hey!)
Let it buzz with the quarters and ones
Whoever's looking, let 'em look
We'll call 'em back when the night is done
Got a jukebox, got a stool, got a long old bar
So put your phone in the tip jar

[Bridge: half-time, whole room singing]
It can wait (it can wait)
It can wait (it can wait)
Every little red dot, every "running late"
It can wait

[Final Chorus: loudest, stomps and claps, fiddle on top]
Put your phone in the tip jar (hey!)
Let it buzz with the quarters and ones
Whoever's looking, let 'em look
We'll call 'em back when the night is done
Got a jukebox, got a stool, got a long old bar
So put your phone in the tip jar

[Outro: guitar and whistle, one phone ringing, spoken]
Darlene, whose is that?
Yours, hon. It's your wife. Go home.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 81 BPM, 4/4 with a lazy swing, A major. A slow, heavy stomp you can sway a full glass to.

VOICE: Male baritone, warm, unhurried and a little tired, nearly talking in the verses. A room of mixed voices shouts 'hey!' and sings the chorus and bridge with him. Two spoken lines at the end, one of them an older woman.

INSTRUMENTS: Strummed acoustic guitar, a whistled tune, boot stomps and handclaps, a fiddle playing the hook, a deep 808 kick under the chorus, upright-sounding bass, light snare, a tambourine.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, guitar, whistle, stomps. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:34 Pre-chorus, fiddle in. 0:46 Chorus 1 with the crowd. 1:10 Verse 2. 1:34 Pre-chorus. 1:46 Chorus 2. 2:10 Bridge, half-time, the whole room. 2:28 Final chorus. 2:54 Outro, a phone rings, two spoken lines, ends on a laugh at 3:08.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 2024 country crossover: roomy acoustic instruments with a modern low end. The crowd is recorded close, like a real bar, not a stadium.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first shouted 'hey!' after the title line at 0:49.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original drowns the week. This one unplugs from it: the thing everyone hands over at the door is the phone, and the song ends by sending him home.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Worn out, relieved, belonging, sent home smiling.
